weapons.name: Power Glove
weapons.status: Default (free) primary [Fan-wiki infobox 'Price: Default']. Shipped in BBR v1.4 (Nov 28, 2012), one of the '6 original weapons' [Fan-wiki]. I saw it as one of two primaries on the 2012 loadout screen, marked 'EQUIPPED' [Observed: File:Power_glove.png, uploaded 2012-11-29]. Charge time went from 1.8 to 1.5 s in BBR 1.4.2 (Mar 1, 2013) [Fan-wiki: BBR Version 1.4.2]. The infobox now lists a 2.25 s charge and charged damage of 50 plus 30-60 AoE, so the stats have drifted [Fan-wiki]. Nothing documents its 2026 status [Unverified].
weapons.official_text: "The precursor to the O.C.O. Glove, this weapon can rapidly fire small orbs of energy. When charged up, it delivers a larger and more destructive orb that explodes on impact. This weapon can HANDle any situation." [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Power_Glove
weapons.mechanics: Semi-automatic and fires energy orbs at 1,400 u/s. An uncharged or partly charged shot does 20 damage on a direct hit, with no AoE. 'Fully charged (indicated by the appearance of a small energy ring formed around the Glove)': a direct hit does 50, plus an AoE burst of 60 within 150 units and 30 at 150-300 units. A dropped charge decays in about 1 s. A charged shot uses up the whole magazine (100 ammo, 3.5 s reload). [Fan-wiki: Power Glove]. The wiki trivia says it was the first BBG weapon with charged and uncharged shots [Fan-wiki]. LOOK [Observed: File:Power_Glove.jpg, File:Power_glove.png]: an oversized pale-grey/white robotic glove with three fingers and a thumb, a glowing cyan hexagonal core on the back of the hand, cyan circuit traces and cyan dots on the fingertips. SkyVu-style concept 'Graham's Self-Enhanced Hand' [Observed: File:Graham_glove.png, provenance Unverified] is a grey mechanical hand with cyan lights. GAP: no source gives the colour of the orb or of the explosion [Unverified]. The cyan palette of the glove is only a lead [Inference].

weapons.name: Gamma Ray
weapons.status: Unlock for 150,000 Joules, level 1 [Fan-wiki]. Shipped in BBR v1.4 (Nov 28, 2012) [Fan-wiki]. It is equipped as the primary in the official 1.4 beta video [Observed: File:Graham-gamma-ray.png, a frame of SkyVu's video U3XDJXo1Ej4]. Reload went from 4.0 to 3.6 s in 1.4.2 [Fan-wiki]. BBG 2.6 (Dec 20, 2013) raised damage from 1 to 2 and cut the clip from 120 to 80 [Fan-wiki: Battle Bears Gold/Versions/2.6, transcribing SkyVu's 2.6 change log]. The current infobox says damage 1 and ammo 100, so the wiki contradicts itself [Fan-wiki]. Clip sizes I saw on screen: 250 in the 2012 beta and 120 in a Jan 2014 fan clip [Observed]. 2026: the official Steam trailer shows Graham using it (see mechanics) [Observed; weapon identification is Inference].
weapons.official_text: "Turn your enemies in to walking explosives with this radioactive ray gun. It does very little damage on initial impact, but once you charge them up all the way...BOOM! The radioactive symbol over their head indicates how charged they are. The bigger they are, the longer it takes to blow them up, however yielding a much larger and more aggressive explosion." [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Gamma_Ray
weapons.mechanics: Automatic, a 'short-ranged constant yellow beam' (range 1,000 units, 0.08 s cooldown) that adds radiation to each target it hits. When radiation reaches the target's maximum health the target 'will die instantly in a relatively large explosion' with a 150-200 unit radius that also hurts nearby players, so suicide is possible. 'The end of the projectile emits a type of smoke-like vapour.' The explosion animation is 'the same as the Piece Maker and Phat Man' and scales with the victim's size. Radiation decays at about 3-5 RP/s once the beam stops. [Fan-wiki: Gamma Ray; Status Effects]. STATUS ICON: 'a yellow circle will appear over the player's head' along with a Geiger-counter ticking that speeds up. The disc loses wedges in 4 stages until only the trefoil remains [Fan-wiki: Status Effects]. The wiki icons go from a full 6-wedge disc (File:Hazard-3.png, 0-24%) to the classic trefoil (File:Hazard-0.png, 75-99%) [Observed]. LOOK [Observed: File:Gamma_ray.png, File:Graham_default.png]: a dark round emitter with a bright green octagonal lens, framed by orange/yellow clamp-like brackets. FIRING [Observed: fan clip 'Gamma Ray Demonstration' by ApplerGamers, https://i.ytimg.com/vi/0GuhKiAnNyc/maxresdefault.jpg]: yellow concentric arc rings ripple from the muzzle with a yellow-green glow, a yellow disc icon sits over the target, and the kill fills the screen with a yellow-white blast. 2026 OFFICIAL TRAILER [Observed: frames I extracted, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-thallo-site/91c60972-6d3f-51de-9a92-c1d563bcf5a4/scratchpad/weapons/dl/graham/trailer/g_007.png to g_014.png, i.e. 8.0-9.75 s of trailer.mp4; same moment as Steam screen_03.jpg]: Graham (rainbow-striped cap skin) fires golden ring arcs. The target glows yellow with white sparkles, and a yellow-and-black trefoil appears over its head at 8.25 s. At 9.0-9.75 s the target bursts into orange body chunks inside a yellow-white explosion cloud, with a white hexagonal shockwave ring on the floor. Other players' pink beams and a white/cyan-lightning flash share the shot. That this kill is the Gamma Ray's radiation detonation is [Inference]. Character card at 11.0 s (t_0023.jpg, g_019.png): an orange blocky housing with vent slots, a black octagonal muzzle ring with orange prongs, a green glowing core and a yellow-white muzzle flash [Observed].
image_leads: File:Gamma Ray Demonstration (YouTube 0GuhKiAnNyc, fan Everyplay clip)

weapons.name: Rivet Gun
weapons.status: Unlock for 50,000 Joules, level 1 [Fan-wiki]. The wiki-transcribed BBR 1.4.3 'coming soon' list (Apr 2013) names it [Fan-wiki: BBR Version 1.4.3], and it appears in the 'BB 1.4.3 COMING SOON' promo art [Observed: File:1.4.3Weapons_B.png]. It was 'delayed to make improvements': it was originally meant to plant rivets linked by beams into a damage barrier. The weapon page says it was 'released in v2.1' (BBG, July 15, 2013), but the Updates log for 2.1 does not list it [Fan-wiki; release version Unverified]. BBG 2.6 changed reload from 6 to 4 s and 'Time to Live' from 10 to 7 s [Fan-wiki: Versions/2.6].
weapons.official_text: "Not just for fixing. This weapon shoots electrified rivets that stick into walls and create a ball of death!" [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Rivet_Gun
weapons.mechanics: Fires rivets at 1,600 u/s, 4 per clip, 1 s rate. Rivets 'land on the ground or any wall and immediately form light purple energy fields around their landing area, which last for 7 seconds. The rivets themselves cannot directly damage players.' Field damage is higher toward the centre (30 DPS). The fields 'are in fact square when viewed from above' despite the 'ball' in the description [Fan-wiki]. LOOK [Observed: File:Rosie.png model turnaround; File:1.4.3Weapons_B.png; File:Rivet_Gun.jpg]: a chunky dark-brown/black boxy gun with orange bands and an orange hazard-symbol decal, a silver cylindrical muzzle (hex/nut-shaped from the front), a black top carry handle and a looped grip. The orange canister props in Rosie.png are probably its rivet magazines [Inference].

weapons.name: Hand Cannon
weapons.status: Unlock for 60 Gas, level 1 ('first Engineer primary weapon to cost Gas') [Fan-wiki]. Added in BBG v2.5 (Nov 27, 2013) [Fan-wiki: Updates]. In 2.6, projectile speed rose from 400 to 750; the infobox now lists 800 u/s [Fan-wiki].
weapons.official_text: "Slow and steady, just like Graham himself. This slow moving missile causes a massive explosion on contact." [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Hand_Cannon
weapons.mechanics: Single slow missile, 2 per clip, 1 s cooldown, 3 s reload. Explodes on contact with a player or surface: 20-40 damage, AoE max 100 / min 300 units, with a high self-damage risk [Fan-wiki]. The projectile is described as 'a comically large green-black missile' [Fan-wiki]. LOOK [Observed: File:Hand_Cannon.png]: a short, fat orange/gold cannon with dark-brown bands and a glowing bright-green octagonal front face, held two-handed at the hip. GAP: no image of the missile in flight or of its explosion [Unverified].

weapons.name: Buzzsaw
weapons.status: Unlock for 60 Gas now, no level lock [Fan-wiki]. Added in BBG v2.6 (Dec 20, 2013) at 80 Gas [Fan-wiki: Versions/2.6].
weapons.official_text: "Gun that shoots spinning saw blades: Check! Spinning saw blades that explode on impact: Check!" [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Buzzsaw
weapons.mechanics: Fires spinning saw blades, 3 per clip, 1 s rate, 70 damage, explosives 35-70, AoE 150/275 units. The blades explode on contact with an opponent. They can 'dig into surfaces and then track the closest opponent' with weak, short-range homing, 'sink below the ground and cease any effect' after a short time, and sometimes 'hover at a spot for several seconds'. Damage stays the same regardless of distance from the blast. The wiki claims it is one of only two projectiles that pass through the Iron Curtain [Fan-wiki]. LOOK [Observed: File:BuzzSaw.jpg]: a dark-grey/black launcher with a green glowing light strip and a large white/silver toothed circular saw blade mounted vertically at the front. GAP: no image of the blade's flight, of it burrowing, or of its explosion [Unverified].

weapons.name: MuskIt
weapons.status: Unlock for 60 Gas, level 10 [Fan-wiki]. Added in BBG v2.12 (Oct 2, 2014) [Fan-wiki: Updates]. It is missing from weapons_by_class.json because its page lacks Category:BBG Weapons. Stats changed: the first wiki revision (2014-10-03) lists radiation 40-60, damage 35, ammo 2 and -5% speed; the current page lists radiation 35.5-55.5, damage 30, ammo 3 and no modifier [Fan-wiki].
weapons.official_text: "The musk of the Gyrnobal has been known to turn people into mutants, but most blow up." [Game text via wiki, spelling 'Gyrnobal' as quoted] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/MuskIt
weapons.mechanics: Shotgun-style. It deals damage and irradiates enemies in a small cone at close range (1.5 s rate, 3 ammo, 4.5 s reload, radiation range 100-150 units). It uses the same radiation status and detonation as the Gamma Ray (see Status Effects) [Fan-wiki]. Visual per wiki: 'When fired, it shoots green stuff of what appears to look like bug spray' [Fan-wiki]. LOOK [Observed: File:Musket.jpg]: a long dark-maroon/brown barrel with white curved bands, a salmon-pink bulbous rear chamber with a grey emblem, a yellow ring, and a yellow canister hanging below. The bug-sprayer reading is [Inference] from the wiki text.

weapons.name: Turret
weapons.status: Default (free) secondary [Fan-wiki], one of the BBR v1.4 originals (Nov 28, 2012) [Fan-wiki; Observed on the 2012 loadout screen, File:Turret.png]. 1.4.2 changes: damage 2.5 to 3.5, dispersion 0.04 to 0.03, health 100 to 135. BBG 2.6 changes: damage 3.5 to 7, range 2000 to 1000 [Fan-wiki]. The current infobox (damage 3.5, health 180, range 1,800) conflicts with those logs [Fan-wiki].
weapons.official_text: "Place this device on the ground while facing the enemy and it will do all the killing for you. Use it wisely, you only get one at a time. If you wish to reposition, you can use the self-destruct to destroy your existing turret." [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Turret
weapons.mechanics: Deployed sentry with 'approximately 2-3 seconds to set up'. It cannot turn and covers a 100-degree cone with unlimited bullets at 0.25 s per shot. It targets one enemy at a time, is not perfectly accurate, and is immune to status effects. When destroyed, 'after two seconds of smoking, it will vanish'. One turret at a time (two with Ammo+2); self-destruct via the reload button [Fan-wiki]. Early wiki text (Nov 2, 2012, pre-release): 'Graham lays the turret on the ground as the turret rises up. It shoots the same bullets as the Electric Honey' [Fan-wiki, early revision]. In the official 1.4 beta video the turret icon sits beside a red self-destruct button and '0/1' ammo [Observed: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/U3XDJXo1Ej4/hq1.jpg, low-res]. LOOK in game [Observed: File:Turretdeploy.png, File:Turret.jpg, File:Turret_2.png]: a white/light-grey boxy gun body with vent grilles and one grey barrel, team-coloured diagonal stripes (blue or red), on a dark X-shaped stand with four square feet. Carried, it reads as a white box with a handle bearing a red light. CONCEPT [Observed: File:Engineer2.png, File:Engineer1.png]: a domed grey turret with glowing red or blue team stripes. The released shape differs [Observed]. GAP: bullet and tracer colour in BBG are undocumented [Unverified].

weapons.name: Proximity Mine
weapons.status: Unlock for 100,000 Joules, level 1 [Fan-wiki]. Added in BBR v1.4, Nov 28, 2012 [Fan-wiki; Observed on the 2012 loadout, File:Proximity_mines.png]. 1.4.2 changes: reload 3.5 to 3.2 s, cooldown 3.0 to 2.8 s, priming 2.5 to 2.2 s. BBG 2.6 changes: AoE radius 100/200 to 150/300 [Fan-wiki]. The 'red button' was later removed and its job moved to the reload button, but the description still mentions it [Fan-wiki].
weapons.official_text: "Useful in high traffic or choke areas, this placable explosive can attach itself to any surface. Once an enemy gets close, it will explode. This weapon can also be remote detonated by tapping the red button by the ammo count." [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Proximity_Mine
weapons.mechanics: Thrown mine that sticks to any surface. It explodes when an enemy steps near it or on remote detonation, and does not explode if detonated before landing. It bounces off a player if thrown directly at one. Explosives 20-110, AoE 140/300 units, self-damage possible, 4 ammo. Enemy explosives can set it off. 'In a later update, a small red line will display above the mine' [Fan-wiki]. LOOK [Observed: File:Proximity_Mine.jpg; File:So_many_mines.jpg; File:Dat_Engineer.jpg]: a dark olive-green/grey four-pointed star or claw-shaped mine with a small green glowing centre. Placed mines carpet floors and walls, each with a thin red vertical line rising from it. DETONATION [Observed, low-res: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/U3XDJXo1Ej4/hq2.jpg, SkyVu's 1.4 beta video]: with the mine icon, a red detonate button and '0/1' on the HUD, a bright white starburst with long white/yellow rays and a yellow puff. That this is the mine going off is [Inference].

weapons.name: Gernobyl
weapons.status: Unlock for 90 Gas, level 1 [Fan-wiki]. Added in BBR v1.4.3 (store notes dated Apr 15, 2013; shipped as 1.4.3.1 on Apr 23, 2013) [Fan-wiki: Updates]. In 2013 its stat panel showed SPEED +5% [Observed: File:Dmimage.jpg]. BBG 2.6 changes: clip 1 to 3, fire rate 1.5 to 1.25, AoE 100/200 to 150/300, radiation minimum 45 to 55, puddle radiation 2 to 10 [Fan-wiki: Versions/2.6].
weapons.official_text: In-game: "Radioactive goo never hurt anyone, unless of course it came from the contaminated mouth of an adorable little mutated mammal. The longer your exposure the greater your chance of death!" [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Gernobyl . App Store patch note, as the wiki transcribes it: "Gernobyl: Engineer's radioactive launcher.This mid-sized rodent shoots irradiated goop: a hit will cause radiation damage and slight physical damage, if you miss an opponent it creates a radioactive puddle- any player who steps in it will receive radiation damage." [Game text via wiki: Updates page]
weapons.mechanics: Arcing glob launcher at 1,000 u/s. It shoots 'irradiating globs of light green goo'. A hit does medium radiation plus some physical damage. A miss leaves a puddle that irradiates anyone who steps in it, and each puddle 'lasts 4.5 seconds'. 'The goo will split into 2 to 3 droplets'. It shares the Gamma Ray's radiation and detonation and was 'designed to complement the Gamma Ray' [Fan-wiki]. LOOK [Observed: File:Gernobyl.jpg, File:Gernobil.jpg 3D turnaround, File:1.4.3Weapons_B.png]: a fat tan/cream gerbil with a brown back stripe and tail, glowing yellow eyes and an open red mouth with buck teeth oozing green goo. It wears a black harness with a yellow-and-black hazard band, has a silver-and-black carry handle on its back, and lime-green goo patches drip from its body. Graham carries it by the handle like a lantern. PROJECTILE [Observed: File:Radioactive_goo.jpeg]: small glowing yellow-green droplets with glowing trails. PUDDLE [Observed: File:Radioactive_puddle.jpeg]: large, flat, opaque lumpy lime/yellow-green goo blobs, with a yellow-and-black trefoil icon on screen. 2026 TRAILER [Observed: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-thallo-site/91c60972-6d3f-51de-9a92-c1d563bcf5a4/scratchpad/weapons/dl/graham/trailer/g_004.png and g_005.png, 7.25-7.5 s]: glowing lime-green blobs fly from Graham toward the target and leave green oval splats on the floor. That these are Gernobyl shots, just before he switches to the Gamma Ray, is [Inference]. CONCEPTS [Observed: Screen_Shot_2013-01-24 and 2013-01-23 files; provenance Unverified]: early ideas were a radiation tube launcher, a canister, an axe and a big gun, before the handle-on-gerbil design.

weapons.name: Black Hole
weapons.status: Unlock for 150,000 Joules, level 15 lock; the first wiki revision (Nov 4, 2014) said 300,000 Joules [Fan-wiki]. No update log names its release. The page was created Nov 4, 2014 and a fan Everyplay clip was published Oct 31, 2014, so it probably arrived around late Oct 2014 [Inference; Unverified]. A design-pick image uploaded Nov 22, 2012 shows four sphere options with the purple swirl circled [Observed: File:Black_Hole_Shot.png; provenance Unverified].
weapons.official_text: "A star that has collapsed in on itself, creating a gravitational force so strong not even light can escape. But Graham is an engineer so don't worry about it." [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Black_Hole
weapons.mechanics: Thrown or fired orb (1,000 u/s, 1 ammo, 2.5 s rate, 3 s reload) that creates an area which 'slows down all the opponents within its Area of Effect, while dealing moderate damage'. Slow 65%, duration 4.0 s (first revision: 5.0 s), about 30 DPS. Self-damage is possible [Fan-wiki]. LOOK [Observed: File:BlackHole.jpg]: a glossy magenta-purple sphere with a darker swirl, held in one hand. IN USE [Observed, low-res fan clip thumbnails https://i.ytimg.com/vi/7gdfSoWC2ZI/hq1.jpg and hq3.jpg]: a small purple orb in flight; the kill frame shows a cyan/teal glow around the victim. The field's shape and colour are not documented [Unverified]. Not listed under the 'Slowed' status, so whether it shows the yellow Z icon is [Unverified].
image_leads: File:Black Hole BBG (YouTube 7gdfSoWC2ZI, fan clip by AM22)

weapons.name: Bind Field (formerly Slow Field)
weapons.status: Unlock for 50,000 Joules, level 1 [Fan-wiki]. Added in BBG v2.6 (Dec 20, 2013) as 'Slow Field' and later renamed 'Bind Field', 'most likely' to avoid confusion with the Slow Motion Field special [Fan-wiki]. It is missing from weapons_by_class.json because its page lacks Category:BBG Weapons.
weapons.official_text: "Make your opponents feel as old as you do. All enemies within the field stop and dream about bingo." [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Bind_Field
weapons.mechanics: Fires 'a prickly purple-green ball in an arc'. On hitting a solid surface (players excluded) it 'detonates and forms a medium-sized force field which slows all opponents caught in its radius by 75% for 3 seconds'. No damage; 1 ammo, 2.5 s rate, 3 s reload [Fan-wiki]. Slowed status: 'a yellow Z will appear over the player's head' (Slow Field is listed) [Fan-wiki: Status Effects]. LOOK [Observed: File:Slowfield.png]: a dark-brown sphere covered in a lime-green line network, with purple spiky hexagonal knobs at the nodes, held in one hand. GAP: the field's colour and shape are not documented [Unverified].

weapons.name: Radiation Rod
weapons.status: Unlock for 75,000 Joules, level 1 [Fan-wiki]. Added in BBG v2.5 (Nov 27, 2013) [Fan-wiki: Updates].
weapons.official_text: "Straight from the core of the Ursa Major. Warning may cause spontaneous bear combustion if in contact for long periods of time." [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Radiation_Rod
weapons.mechanics: A 'placeable nuclear fuel rod that creates a glowing radiation field when placed'. It irradiates enemies inside at 60 radiation/s for 10 s, which is the fastest radiation in the game, and blocks Sniper lock-ons. 5 rods, 1 s between placements. A fully irradiated enemy explodes (blast radius 150-200 units, sized by the victim's maximum health) using the same yellow-disc and Geiger-tick status as the Gamma Ray. The owner is immune to his own radiation but not to the blast [Fan-wiki]. LOOK [Observed: File:Radiation_Rod.png]: a purple cylindrical canister with lime-green chevron stripes, a radiation-trefoil decal and a glowing green vented end cap, held at the hip. GAP: the field's glow colour and radius visuals are not documented [Unverified].

weapons.name: Dragon Slayzer (BBG)
weapons.status: Unlock for 400,000 Joules, no level lock [Fan-wiki stub]. Added in BBG v2.51 (Apr 13, 2018): 'New weapon for Engineer (BBG) - the Dragon Slayzer (BBG)' [Fan-wiki: Updates]. A different Dragon Slayzer exists in Battle Bears Overclock (BBO) as Oliver's weapon [Fan-wiki].
weapons.official_text: none found (the BBG wiki page is a stub with no quoted description). BBO-era page gives only a fan description.
weapons.mechanics: BBG stats only [Fan-wiki infobox]: explosives 10-20, 'Duration 4 seconds' (the effect is unnamed), damage 35, 1 s cooldown, 4 ammo, 4 s reload, projectile 800 u/s. Nothing documents what it fires in BBG [Unverified]. LOOK [Observed: File:DragonSlayzer(BBG).jpeg, uploaded 2018-05-12]: a handheld red dragon head with green eyes, white teeth and spikes, small red horns and wings, and a long silver double-edged blade coming out of its mouth. BBO version (different game) [Fan-wiki: Dragon Slayzer]: 'a dragon with a sword coming out of its head. The laser, which the dragon fires, is an orange blast. The dragon's color is red'; 'fires a straight-moving laser that explodes on contact' with splash damage. BBO art [Observed: File:DSNew.jpg; File:Image-1.jpg, labelled 'THE DRAGON SLAYZER']: a grey/silver dragon head with a blade from the mouth. That the BBG model reuses the BBO design is [Inference]; that it fires the same orange exploding laser is [Unverified]. The stub's only file, File:Huggable-suction-pose.png, is an unrelated template artefact.

weapons.name: T Square
weapons.status: Default (free) melee [Fan-wiki]. One of the BBR v1.4 originals, Nov 28, 2012 [Fan-wiki; Observed on the 2012 loadout, File:Wrench.png list]. BBG 2.6 cut Melee+1 from 8 to 5 [Fan-wiki].
weapons.official_text: "Tee off on your opponents with this classic tool. Ouch." [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/T_Square
weapons.mechanics: Melee swing, 55 damage, no stat modifier [Fan-wiki]. Class page: Engineer melees have 'fast draw times' [Fan-wiki]. LOOK [Observed: File:T_Square.jpg; HUD icon in File:Graham-gamma-ray.png]: a long silver/light-grey ruler blade with black tick marks and a dark, slightly curved crossbar head. The final concept art shows Graham holding a ruler-like silver tool [Observed: File:Graham_concept_art.jpg]. He also leans on a T-square on the BBF card [Observed in prior research: File:Graham_BBF.jpg].

weapons.name: Wrench
weapons.status: Unlock for 45,000 Joules, no level lock [Fan-wiki]. Added in BBR v1.4, Nov 28, 2012 [Fan-wiki; Observed as 'WRENCH EQUIPPED' on the 2012 loadout, File:Wrench.png]. Before 2.6 it had no stat modifier; 2.6 added +10% Speed and cut Melee+1 from 7 to 5 [Fan-wiki].
weapons.official_text: "Just a trusty monkey wrench. This will fix your enemies real good." [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Wrench
weapons.mechanics: Melee swing, 30 damage, +10% speed; 'It makes metal noises when used' [Fan-wiki]. LOOK [Observed: File:Screen_Shot_2012-12-09_at_10.11.21_AM.png; File:Wrench.png; HUD icon in File:Radioactive_puddle.jpeg]: a big orange pipe wrench with a dark-grey adjustable jaw. The wiki notes it is 'actually a pipe wrench' despite the 'monkey wrench' text [Fan-wiki]; the images agree [Observed].

weapons.name: Double Wrench
weapons.status: Unlock for 140,000 Joules, level 10 lock [Fan-wiki]. Added in BBG v2.12 (Oct 2, 2014) [Fan-wiki: Updates]. Stats changed: the first wiki revision listed 37 damage, +20% special speed and -10% speed; the current page lists 30 damage and +30% special speed [Fan-wiki].
weapons.official_text: "Prepare for trouble and make it double... wrench." [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Double_Wrench
weapons.mechanics: Melee swing, 30 damage, +30% special (cooldown) speed [Fan-wiki]. Wiki trivia: 'The wrench depicted in game is an open end wrench' with different-sized jaws at each end [Fan-wiki]. GAP: no image of it found on the wiki [Unverified]. The JustNubz 2026 showcase, Engineer chapter at 34:42, is the best lead for its look.
image_leads: none on wiki; lead: JustNubz showcase https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-lAtv-j9Sms at 34:42-39:57 (not viewable from sandbox)

weapons.name: Crowbar
weapons.status: Unlock for 150,000 Joules, no level lock [Fan-wiki]. Added in BBG v2.21 (July 3, 2015) with other melees [Fan-wiki: Updates].
weapons.official_text: "One of Graham's many unusual tools. A crow infused with a steel bar after radiation testing." [Game text via wiki] https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Crowbar
weapons.mechanics: Melee swing, 55 damage (the Engineer's highest), +15% health [Fan-wiki]. LOOK [Observed: File:Image9.PNG, shown on White Graham]: a purple crowbar whose hooked end is a crow's head, with dark-purple spiky feathers, a tan/orange beak and a pale eye.

notes:
CLASS-LEVEL FINDINGS
- Full BBG arsenal has 17 weapons (6 primaries, 7 secondaries, 4 melees) per the class page Engineer (BBG) [Fan-wiki].
- weapons_by_class.json["Graham"] has only 15. It misses MuskIt and Bind Field because their pages lack Category:BBG Weapons. The "/Weapons" subpage is an empty stub.
- None of the 5 "_unassigned" pages belongs to Graham. Hazard Toy is Assassin [Fan-wiki].
- Class data, from Template:Class:Engineer (BBG) [Game text via wiki]: "Don't be fooled by his bushy gray mustache, this class relies more on brains than brawn or speed. This wise whiskered bear specializes in defending areas of the map and controlling enemy traffic."
  - Health 120; forward speed 250 (2.6 raised base speed from 200 to 250); price 100 Gas [Fan-wiki].

  - BBG 2.1 (Jul 2013): Rivet Gun, per its page only
  - BBG 2.5 (Nov 27, 2013): Hand Cannon and Radiation Rod
  - BBG 2.6 (Dec 20, 2013): Buzzsaw and Slow Field (later renamed Bind Field), plus broad rebalances
  - BBG 2.12 (Oct 2, 2014): MuskIt and Double Wrench
  - About Oct-Nov 2014: Black Hole [Inference]
  - BBG 2.21 (Jul 3, 2015): Crowbar
  - BBG 2.51 (Apr 13, 2018): Dragon Slayzer
